clue.text: Subject of Geography left out for a term …

indicators.note: something that is out is no longer there, so that letter is dropped from the subject

parts.note: geography is the study of the world
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A school subject has been dropped from the timetable for a whole term.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the L out of WORLD leaves WORD. This starts a word ladder, and the trailing dots lead on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A word is a single unit of language, and 'term' is a common synonym for one.

clue.text: Responsibility of The Guardian to illustrate reflectively

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things back to front, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: to illustrate is to draw

explanation.surface: The Guardian newspaper is told it has a duty to illustrate its stories thoughtfully.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital T makes 'The Guardian' look like the newspaper, but any guardian will do.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal ward is a child or person placed under the protection and care of a guardian.

clue.text: Badly want to displace Conservative party

indicators.note: displacing something moves it out of where it was, so that letter is removed

parts.note: to crave is to want badly
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: Someone is desperate to see a rival party push the Conservatives out of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conservative party' reads as one political phrase, but the party is the definition and Conservative is just its initial.
explanation.definitionFit: A rave is a large lively party, especially an all-night dance event with electronic music.

clue.text: … which sees head becoming Latin master …

indicators.note: the head is the first letter, and becoming says it turns into something else

parts.note: the leading dots carry on from 1 across, so 'which' stands for that answer
L is the abbreviation for Latin

explanation.surface: A term in which a headmaster is replaced by a Latin master.
explanation.walkthrough: WORD has its first letter changed to L to give LORD, the next rung of the word ladder.
explanation.definitionFit: A lord is a ruler or master, as in lord and master, someone holding authority over others.

clue.text: Some nerve — keeping time like a diva

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: the optic nerve is one kind of nerve
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: It takes some nerve to keep everyone waiting the way a diva does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some nerve' sounds like cheek, but it means one particular nerve, the one serving the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a celebrated female opera singer, so behaving like one is operatic, theatrical and dramatic.

clue.text: Fried fish starter, battered to provide contrast

indicators.note: something battered is knocked about out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of fish

explanation.surface: A cook offers battered fried fish as a starter to vary the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fried fish' and 'battered' read as a chip-shop order, but battered is the signal to rearrange FRIED plus F.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that differ are unlike one another, so they stand in contrast when compared.

clue.text: … but English covering the last lessons of History?

indicators.note: covering the final letter hides it under another one, which takes its place

parts.note: the leading dots carry on from 3 across, whose answer is the starting word
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A school timetable where English lessons have crowded out the final History classes.
explanation.walkthrough: The D at the end of LORD is replaced by E, the next rung of the ladder.
explanation.definitionFit: Lore is traditional knowledge handed down through generations, the teachings a people learns from its past.

clue.text: Look and place letter R down first (it's representative of King)

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look, as in lo and behold
taken as written
D is the abbreviation for down
lieu means place, as in 'in lieu of'
the setter reads letter as someone involved in a let, an occupant renting a property

explanation.surface: Instructions for a crossword grid: look, then write the letter R in the down light first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts the look, the R and the down ahead of the rest. A Lord Lieutenant is the monarch's personal representative in each county of the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: The holder of this office stands in for the sovereign at ceremonies and official events across a county.

clue.text: Think again about scattering paper on hike

indicators.note: scattering throws things about in all directions, so the letters end up in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a hike is a raise, as in a pay hike

explanation.surface: A walker reconsiders dropping litter along a country walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hike' suggests a walk, but it is a rise in pay or price.
explanation.definitionFit: To reappraise is to assess something anew, reconsidering a judgement already made.

clue.text: Put out hip brought together with nice manoeuvring internally

parts.note: hip means fashionable, which is in

indicators.note: internally means on the inside, so the rearranged letters go within the other word

parts.note: convened means assembled or brought together

indicators.note: manoeuvring moves things around into new positions, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's hip is dislocated during a supposedly nice bit of internal manipulation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' suggests a dislocated hip, but hip is the slang for fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Being put out means being bothered or troubled, which is what an inconvenienced person feels.

clue.text: The only league on Earth

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for league
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for Earth

explanation.surface: A boast that this is the only sporting league anywhere on the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Lone means single or solitary, as in 'the lone survivor', meaning the only one left.

clue.text: Space for Divinity to provide income

parts.note: RE is religious education, the school subject also called divinity
a venue is a space where events are held

explanation.surface: A church hall is rented out to bring in money for the divinity school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' puts the space after the subject. RE is religious education, a British school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Revenue is the money an organisation or government takes in, its income.

clue.text: Position of fascists in the past — it's a mixed bag

parts.note: fascists are on the far right, written FAR R with R for right
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: A historian sums up the old fascist movement's political stance as a jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrago is a confused mixture or hotchpotch of things, the same idea as a mixed bag.

clue.text: Chaos of latest police blackout

indicators.note: chaos is complete disorder, so the letters that follow are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The most recent police news blackout has caused chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blackout' reads as a press embargo, but here it is the sky going dark.
explanation.definitionFit: When the moon fully covers the sun, daylight is blacked out for a few minutes.

clue.text: One used to spell with with with with

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with
with and and both mean together alongside

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson on the right tool for spelling a word with too many withs.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue repeats 'with' four times: one belongs to the definition, one gives W, one is the joining word meaning alongside, and the last gives AND.
explanation.definitionFit: A wizard or magician casts spells by waving a magic stick, the tool spells are made with.

clue.text: Scent of female led soldier to get brief attack of nerves

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female
to run something is to lead it
a GI is an American soldier
a panic attack is a sudden attack of nerves

explanation.surface: A woman's perfume leaves the soldier she leads briefly flustered.
explanation.walkthrough: PANIC loses its last letter to give PANI.
explanation.definitionFit: Frangipani is a tropical flowering tree whose fragrant blossoms give a perfume of the same name.

clue.text: Curries regularly kept by French to have later

indicators.note: something kept by another is held inside it

parts.note: avoir is the French verb meaning to have

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of curries

explanation.surface: Leftover curries are saved by a French cook to eat later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to have later' sounds like saving food for afterwards; 'to have' belongs with French, and 'later' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Au revoir is the French farewell, used like the casual English goodbye 'later!' or 'see you'.

clue.text: Make Manx soldiers dedicated to duty

definitions.meaning: first meaning: cut off the tail, since a Manx cat is born without one
second meaning: a small squad assigned to a particular task

explanation.surface: A call to turn the soldiers of the Isle of Man into a dedicated force.
explanation.walkthrough: Manx means from the Isle of Man, but the Manx cat is famously tailless, so making something Manx means removing its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting off a tail can be read as de-tail; separately, a military detail is a group posted to a specific job.

clue.text: Extended overhaul to maintain big ends

indicators.note: the ends of words are their final letters, so those are kept

parts.note: the final letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A mechanic recommends an extended overhaul to keep a car's big ends in order.
explanation.walkthrough: Big ends are the bearings at the end of an engine's connecting rods, which makes the phrase look like a single car part.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extended has been made greater in length or duration, stretched out.

clue.text: Get money from the rich? Ultimately the opposite here

definitions.text: Get money from the rich? Ultimately the opposite here

parts.note: surface reading: a Robin Hood scheme to make the wealthy pay up, the very definition of a levy on them
setter's reading: the levy word comes first, but in the end this is a refuge where the rich keep their money and avoid paying

explanation.walkthrough: The first part reads as the levy word itself; the second says this place does the reverse, sheltering the wealth of the rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Offshore jurisdictions with very low rates attract wealthy people to keep their money there and avoid paying at home.

clue.text: England's back batting twice before finally bowling and taking lunch

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of England
a side that is batting is in, and twice doubles it

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the next word

parts.note: the last letter of bowling

explanation.surface: A cricket report: England's tail-ender bats twice before the bowlers break for lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batting side is said to be 'in', and a back is a defensive player, which gives the surface its sporting flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: Dining means eating a meal, so someone taking lunch is dining.

clue.text: Massive fan of Italian cheese — if it's brought back for me

indicators.note: bringing something back returns it the way it came, so it is read backwards
for here means in place of, so one pair of letters swaps in for another

parts.note: Parmesan is a hard Italian cheese
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A huge cheese lover asks for the Parmesan to be passed back to them.
explanation.walkthrough: The ME in PARMESAN is swapped for IT reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan is a strongly committed supporter of a cause or party, an ardent follower.

clue.text: Run after one across the boundary here!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a run in tights or stockings, a line of unravelled stitches
second meaning: the thing used to climb over a wall; read after 1 across it also names this puzzle's theme around the grid's edge

explanation.surface: A cricketer runs after the ball as it crosses the boundary rope.
explanation.walkthrough: Placed after WORD, the answer to 1 across, it makes WORD LADDER: the across answers round the edge of the grid change one letter at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: British English calls a run in tights a ladder, and climbers use one to get over a wall.

clue.text: Scrappy win was eighth attempt at covering up problems

indicators.note: something scrappy is untidy and disorganised, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A team scraped a win, its eighth go at papering over its troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a whitewash is winning every match of a series, which the sporting surface hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitewashing means concealing faults or wrongdoing, like painting over a stained wall to hide the marks.

clue.text: Opportunity to get 33% reduction in unwanted gas

indicators.note: a reduction by a third means one third of the letters are cut away

parts.note: a window is an opportunity, as in a window of opportunity

explanation.surface: A chance to cut emissions of unwanted gases by a third.
explanation.walkthrough: A third of six letters is two, so the last two letters, OW, go.
explanation.definitionFit: Wind means flatulence, gas in the gut that a person would rather not have.

clue.text: Obama extremely content to leave Honolulu where it is

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its outermost letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of Obama

indicators.note: when the contents leave, only the outer shell of the word remains

parts.note: the first and last letters of Honolulu

explanation.surface: Obama, born in Honolulu, is very happy to leave the city where it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' in the definition refers back to Honolulu, Hawaii's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Honolulu stands on the Hawaiian island of Oahu, so the island is the place where the city is.

clue.text: Held on, ignoring the cold for a breather

indicators.note: ignoring something leaves it out of account, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: clung means held on tightly
C is the abbreviation for cold

explanation.surface: A climber clings on, ignoring the freezing weather, to snatch a breather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breather' suggests a rest, but here it is the organ that breathes.
explanation.definitionFit: Lungs are the organs used for respiration, so one may be called a breather.

clue.text: Sister introduces a discontented combative daughter as 'a bit different'

indicators.note: to introduce something is to bring it inside, so the sister holds the next letter

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister
taken as written

indicators.note: without its contents a word keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of combative
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A nun presents her unhappy, quarrelsome daughter as slightly unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nuanced has subtle shades of difference, slight distinctions rather than stark ones.

clue.text: State of Virginia getting new union at university

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for Virginia
N is the abbreviation for new
U is the abbreviation for union
taken as written
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: The state of Virginia sets up a new students' union at its university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State of Virginia' looks like a US state, but the state is a country in the Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanuatu is an independent island nation in the South Pacific, a sovereign state.

clue.text: Outer layer in between radius and diameter…

indicators.note: between means flanked on both sides, so the short word sits inside the two letters

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for radius
taken as written
D is the abbreviation for diameter

explanation.surface: A geometry lesson on the outer layer lying between radius and diameter.
explanation.walkthrough: This starts a second word ladder, led on by the trailing dots.
explanation.definitionFit: Rind is the tough outer skin of fruit, cheese or bacon, a covering layer.

clue.text: … minus end and start of great circle …

indicators.note: minus means taken away, and the end is the final letter

parts.note: the leading dots carry on from 27 across, whose answer is the starting word

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of great

explanation.surface: A geometry lesson continued: take away the end and start drawing a great circle.
explanation.walkthrough: RIND loses its D and gains G.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring is a circular band or shape, so it is another word for a circle.

clue.text: … needs 21st in series for one part of 21?

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one letter swaps in where another stood

parts.note: the leading dots carry on from 28 across, whose answer is the starting word
U is the twenty-first letter of the alphabet
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A puzzle asking which part of the series is needed to complete a sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: The I in RING becomes U. 21 down is LADDER, and each step in this ladder of words is one of these.
explanation.definitionFit: A rung is one of the crosspieces you step on when climbing a ladder.
